statement: Let a path be a finite sequence of L/R choices. A path p exists in a tree t if following p from the root reaches a Node, and val_t(p) is that node's i64 value. The function returns a result r (not a failure) such that: (i) for every path p, p exists in root if and only if p exists in r; (ii) for every path p that exists in root, val_r(p) equals the sum of val_root(q) over all paths q that exist in root and satisfy val_root(q) >= val_root(p).
preconditions: root is a valid binary search tree: for every node, all values in its left subtree are strictly less than the node's value, all values in its right subtree are strictly greater than the node's value, and both subtrees are valid BSTs; all node values in root are distinct; the number of nodes in root is between 0 and 10000 inclusive; every node value is between -10000 and 10000 inclusive.

statement: The function returns a result r (not a failure) and r has exactly the same tree shape as root: for every finite path p over L/R, p exists in root if and only if p exists in r. Equivalently, r is Null exactly when root is Null, and the two trees have the same number of nodes in every corresponding subtree.
